- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then gradually converges toward true values — suggest adjusting initial forecast upward by 1–2% for short-term (0–7 day) horizons.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >90), model tends to overshoot and overcorrect, leading to prolonged overestimation — apply a “cool-down” rule: if forecast > 92 and true < 88, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: forecasts drift upward while true values show downward momentum — if 30-day history shows declining trend, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day.
- Model fails to capture sudden downward corrections after mid-forecast — if true outcome drops >5% from forecast midpoint, adjust forecast downward by 2–4% for next 3 days.
- Model underestimates true volatility in late forecast (last 7–10 days) — if true outcome shows >10% volatility, increase forecast variance by 0.5–1.0% per day for next 5 days.
